roles.drugs: Start as soon as blood cultures are drawn, before LP or CT. 3 months–50 years: ceftriaxone or cefotaxime + vancomycin
>50 years: ceftriaxone or cefotaxime + ampicillin (Listeria) + vancomycin

Neonates <1 month (S. agalactiae, E. coli, Listeria): ampicillin + gentamicin; add cefotaxime if gram-negative meningitis is suspected (MSD). Ceftriaxone is contraindicated in hyperbilirubinemic neonates and those needing calcium-containing IV solutions (bilirubin displacement; ceftriaxone-calcium precipitation) (MSD; FDA label)
Neonates <1 month: ampicillin + cefotaxime (MSD: empiric ampicillin plus gentamicin, cefotaxime, or both)
Neonates, if no cefotaxime: cefepime or ceftazidime (alternatives to cefotaxime for gram-negative infections in neonates)

sources.name: Ngo S, Weeda E, Malloy K. Comparison of Outcomes in Neonates Receiving Cefepime or Ceftazidime. J Pediatr Pharmacol Ther 2023;28(5):439-445
sources.org: Journal of Pediatric Pharmacology and Therapeutics

roles.drugs: After neurosurgery or shunt: vancomycin + an antipseudomonal cephalosporin (cefepime or ceftazidime)
Start as soon as blood cultures are drawn, before LP or CT. 3 months–50 years: ceftriaxone or cefotaxime + vancomycin
>50 years: ceftriaxone or cefotaxime + ampicillin (Listeria) + vancomycin
After neurosurgery or shunt: vancomycin + an antipseudomonal beta-lactam (cefepime, ceftazidime or meropenem)
>50 years: ceftriaxone or cefotaxime + ampicillin (Listeria) + vancomycin

Ceftriaxone is contraindicated in hyperbilirubinemic neonates and those needing calcium-containing IV solutions (bilirubin displacement; ceftriaxone-calcium precipitation) (MSD; FDA label)
Neonates <1 month: ampicillin + cefotaxime (MSD: empiric ampicillin plus gentamicin, cefotaxime, or both)

Neonates <1 month (S. agalactiae, E. coli, Listeria): ampicillin + gentamicin; add cefotaxime if gram-negative meningitis is suspected (MSD). Ceftriaxone is contraindicated in hyperbilirubinemic neonates and those needing calcium-containing IV solutions (bilirubin displacement; ceftriaxone-calcium precipitation) (MSD; FDA label)
Add acyclovir empirically: HSV encephalitis can mimic early bacterial meningitis
After neurosurgery or shunt: vancomycin + meropenem
Dexamethasone just before or with the first antibiotic dose
